items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Wee Bonnie Baker-- came up singing 'Oh Johnny', and took over all the record sales for six weeks.

ctx.x: business, too, though. Those are the kinds of things that come up.

I remember years ago, that song, a girl came up with, singing 'Oh Johnny', with Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw riding the crest -- that little girl came up--Wee Bonnie Baker-- came up singing 'Oh Johnny', and took over all the record sales for six weeks. Nobody was even talking about Benny Goodman while this girl was singing 'Oh Johnny', that song. But you see, those kinds of things happen in this business. 'The Music Goes Round and Round', the jazz world of the early thirties.

But those things, see, they flare up like a big rocket and they flare right down -- for six weeks or so, just like Tiny Tim, you know, and it's a temporary thing. It's hard to repeat; it's hard for Tiny Tim to establish a career doing that, that was a one time thing -- 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips'. It's not a solid thing like jazz is, real jazz or classical music, that carries you on, it never hits a giant sale like 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips.' No jazz record would ever sell like that, I guess, but it will go on…
